doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

chapter: The Philly Sound and its makers
title: Early hip hop and what keeps Gold working
summary: Gold was not surprised by rap's rise, worked on early hip hop records, and still loves working with young songwriters.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Indeed. It seems that technology and hip hop seem to go hand—in—hand with the production values. I wonder if you as a musician yourself was a bit surprised when melodic content became not necessary?

Yeah. But it was a slow ball. It wasn't like it was a fast ball. It started like in the early '80s. Late '70s already you had like the early rap songs coming out. So I knew, and then there were the DJs on the radio that all they all rhymed. Remember the old DJs? I mean the R&B DJs? They were all like poets and didn't know it. Look at Muhammad Ali. Muhammad Ali came out of that same school. Everything was a rhyme. Everything was a phrase that you could remember. So that didn't surprise me, especially being a student of black culture and black music, which I pride myself in those days. It's hard to keep up these days, at age 77. It is. I almost like want to throw my hands up a little bit. But back in those days I definitely, even in the early '80s you know there were a lot of early hip hop records that my partner and I, we worked on behind the scenes, nobody even knew.
Huh. What makes you keep going? © Fillius Jazz Archive 11

I like working, I like music, I like — been doing this since I was a little boy. It's the thing I do best actually I think. I think at this point I do this better than playing the cello even though at one time I think I played the cello better than I did this. So I think what happened was they got reversed. And I'm always fascinated, like this year I guess I can say I did a really nice song with Ed Sheeran that'll come out in September. It's like sort of like a wedding song in an R&B style and it was a good song. And I did another really nice song with — I did a couple of other songs, I can't even remember — well Bruno Mars, you know I mean I'm not even supposed to say that out loud because I signed these agreements that I'm not allowed to even talk about it. But you know these kids, some of them are really super talented songwriters, as good as all the people I used to grow up with.
